body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 25a7b5248cfcc8f3abdaa8daded8a4553133856d -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (with the hands-on 5-axis check the PR itself flags).

Thanks @mkinney, a careful change.

**What looks good**
- `stamp_rise.rs` is conservative: it refuses unless the station is a straight Z feed, the held pose is a lean at or above level, the end is past the contact band, the ball never nears the part more than at the start, and `flank_clear` holds at every half-radius sample. Everything else keeps the old upright feed, so the old behaviour is the fallback.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`; the one cast (`stamp_rise.rs` `ceil() as usize`) is clamped to 1..=4096 and the inputs are checked finite first. The empty-mesh case is refused (tested).
- No verifier law was loosened; the posed-rapid solid law still judges the new held-pose rise. Pins were lowered, not raised. Layering, provenance line, file sizes (156 / 294 / 314 lines), no new dependencies, no build.rs/.github/scripts touched, no CHANGELOG edit, decision file present, body has Changelog and Fixes.

**Local results (PR trial-merged with current main, clean merge, own target dir)**
| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --no-run` | ok |
| motion `swarf_pose_continuity` | 6 passed |
| motion `swarf_reentry` | 2 passed |
| motion `ruling` | 10 passed |
| motion `pivot5d` | 7 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane) |
| motion `--lib multiaxis` | 64 passed |
| app `operations` swarf filter (incl. `swarf_generates_blade_lying_axes_and_verifies_clean`) | all passed, 2 heavy `_full_band` ignored |
| app `advanced_swarf_adds_the_coarse_rungs` | passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the release-mode heavy lanes.

**Requested before merge**
None in code.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- This changes posted 5-axis swarf G-code (a G0 rise at the lying A/B/C angles instead of retract, swing, re-plunge). No golden covers it and the contributor has no 5-axis machine, so a controller or simulator run of a swarf program before it ships is the maintainer's call.
- `rapid_rise` samples the flank every half radius; the sample spacing is the only gap between samples, and the solid law covers the rest.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
